chunks.title: Load
chunks.text: Load sharp knives with the handles up.

chunks.title: Load
chunks.text: Place sharp items so they cannot touch or damage the door seal.

chunks.title: Load
chunks.text: Plastic: only items marked dishwasher safe.

chunks.title: Load
chunks.text: Do not sit, stand or lean on the open door or the racks.

chunks.title: Detergent and rinse aid
chunks.text: Use only dishwasher detergent. Premeasured tablets or packs are recommended.

chunks.title: Detergent and rinse aid
chunks.text: Rinse aid is needed for dry dishes and to limit hard-water spots. Keep it filled.

chunks.title: Detergent and rinse aid
chunks.text: The detergent cup and rinse aid cap are on the inside of the door (location to confirm with property management).

chunks.title: Start
chunks.text: Choose a cycle on the control panel, for example Normal. Not sure which one? Ask property management.

chunks.title: Start
chunks.text: Press Start/Resume, then close the door within 4 seconds.

chunks.title: Start
chunks.text: Start/Resume light flashing: the door was not closed in time. Press Start/Resume again and close the door.

chunks.title: Start
chunks.text: Adding a dish during a cycle: add it, press Start/Resume and close the door within 4 seconds.

chunks.title: What to expect
chunks.text: A load usually takes 2 to 5 hours. This is normal: it saves energy.

chunks.title: What to expect
chunks.text: The first cycle may run longer. Some options can make a cycle longer than 3.5 hours.

chunks.title: What to expect
chunks.text: Hot water not used for 2 weeks or more? Before using the dishwasher, run every hot tap for a few minutes. No smoking or open flame while you do this (hydrogen gas risk).

chunks.title: Outside and inside
chunks.text: Outside: soft damp cloth and mild detergent only. No abrasive cleaners (stainless doors may have a fingerprint-resistant coating).

chunks.title: Outside and inside
chunks.text: Once a month: run a dishwasher cleaner such as affresh®, following the package directions.

chunks.title: Outside and inside
chunks.text: White residue: place (do not pour) 2 cups (500 mL) white vinegar in a glass or dishwasher-safe cup on the bottom rack. Run a full cycle with an air-dry or energy-saving dry option and no detergent.

chunks.title: Clean the filters
chunks.text: How often: every 2 months if you only scrape plates; every 4 months to once a year if you rinse them first. White residue (hard water): once a month.

chunks.title: Clean the filters
chunks.text: Turn the upper filter 1/4 turn counterclockwise and lift it out.

chunks.title: Clean the filters
chunks.text: Gently pull the upper filter assembly apart.

chunks.title: Rinse and put back
chunks.text: Rinse the filters under running water until most soil is gone.

chunks.title: Rinse and put back
chunks.text: Hard soil or white deposits: use a soft brush.

chunks.title: Rinse and put back
chunks.text: Put the filters back fully before the next cycle.

chunks.title: Rinse aid, salt, time away
chunks.text: Keep rinse aid filled for dry dishes.

chunks.title: Rinse aid, salt, time away
chunks.text: Low-salt light (some models): refill with dishwasher softener salt only. Remove the lower rack, unscrew the cap, fill to the edge with the funnel, wipe away salt and screw the cap on tightly. Run a cycle right away. Unsure? Contact property management.

chunks.title: Rinse aid, salt, time away
chunks.text: Away for a long time, or risk of freezing: tell property management.

chunks.title: Won't start
chunks.text: Close the door tightly until it latches.

chunks.title: Won't start
chunks.text: Press Start/Resume, then close the door within 4 seconds. Light flashing: press Start/Resume again and close the door.

chunks.title: Won't start
chunks.text: Check that a cycle was chosen.

chunks.title: Won't start
chunks.text: Still nothing: the breaker or water may be off. Contact property management.

chunks.title: Long cycles, wet or spotty
chunks.text: 2 to 5 hours is normal. The first cycle and some options take longer.

chunks.title: Long cycles, wet or spotty
chunks.text: Wet dishes: fill the rinse aid.

chunks.title: Long cycles, wet or spotty
chunks.text: White spots or residue: hard water. Clean the filters monthly and run a dishwasher cleaner or vinegar rinse (see Appliance Care). Tell property management if it continues.

chunks.title: Water or drain codes
chunks.text: H2O: no water reaching the dishwasher. Contact property management to check the water supply. When it is fixed, press Start/Resume.

chunks.title: Water or drain codes
chunks.text: F9E1: will not drain. Contact property management (the drain hose or disposal connection may need checking).

chunks.title: Water or drain codes
chunks.text: F1E1, F1E5, F8E4, F8E5: follow the IMPORTANT box above.

chunks.title: Other codes and blinking lights
chunks.text: F1E2, F6E1, F7E2, F7E3, F9E3: the dishwasher needs service. Contact property management.

chunks.title: Other codes and blinking lights
chunks.text: No display? The same faults show as blinking lights, for example 8 blinks, pause, 1 blink = H2O. Count the blinks and tell property management.

chunks.title: Other codes and blinking lights
chunks.text: Press Cancel once to stop an alarm sound.

6 Cleaning Instructions IMPORTANT: Do not use wire brush, scouring pad, etc., as they may damage the filters. Rinse filter under running water until most soils are removed. If you have hard-to-remove soils or calcium deposits from hard water, a soft brush may be required. For Professional Installers Turn off water to unit (if possible). Turn off power to unit. If the water cannot be turned off, DO NOT turn off power and keep door closed. Press Cancel key one time to silence alarm tone. Call service.

For Self Installers n Press CANCEL button twice or cycle power. This may clear the issue. n Check to see if the wire connector is connected to the float switch on the drip tray. If the wire is off, reconnect and then hit the cancel button twice. n Check to see if there is any water in the drip tray. If water is in the drip tray, remove the water and reinstall the drip tray. Make sure to connect the wiring to the float. Check to see where water may have leaked into the drip tray (Check the water inlet fittings to see if they are leaking). n If water was in the tray and no leaks were found, run the product on the shortest installation cycle while checking for leaks. The access panel should be off to observe any leaks. n If problem still exists, call for service.

Using a paper towel or cloth, press along the front surface of the T-Gasket to ensure it is flushed well. Check Operation n Read the dishwasher Quick Start Guide that came with your dishwasher. n Check that all parts have been installed and no steps were skipped.

If the dishwasher is not working properly, disconnect power or unplug dishwasher and refer to the “If Dishwasher Does Not Operate” section. If Dishwasher Does Not Operate First try the solutions suggested here to possibly avoid the cost of a service call. n Has the circuit breaker tripped or the house fuse blown? n Is the door closed tightly and latched? n Has the cycle been set correctly to start the dishwasher? n Is the water turned on?
If none of these possible solutions work, refer to the contact information referenced in your Quick Start Guide.

Additional Tips Expect longer wash times. Your new dishwasher will average 2–5 hours per load but use nearly 40% less energy than older models. Designed with a low-wattage, low-energy-consumption motor, your dishwasher washes longer to ensure exceptional cleaning. Certain models are equipped with an optical water sensor, so the first cycle will run longer to calibrate the optical sensor. Selecting certain options could increase cycle time past 3.5 hours.

Rinse aid is necessary for good drying results: This dishwasher is designed to be used with rinse aid for good drying performance and controlling hard-water-deposit buildup. Energy-efficient dishwashers use less water and energy, so they depend on the water sheeting action of rinse aid for good drying performance. Start/Resume light may flash:

When pressing Start/Resume, you must make sure the door is closed within 4 seconds. If you do not close the door within 4 seconds, the Start/Resume light will flash until you press it again. (You must also do this when adding a dish during the middle of a cycle.)
